essentials/festival.local-events.md:
# Local events

Events that already run in the neighbourhood, from the community centre's noticeboard.

- Common Ground Café: a drop-in café every Tuesday at the community centre.
- Elm Street Market: a craft market on the first Saturday of each month.
- Riverside Summer Fair: the primary school's own fair, every July.
- Green Lane Clean-up: a litter pick each spring.
- Harbour Lights Walk: an evening lantern walk in December.
essentials/festival.grant-criteria.md:
# Council small grants

Grants of up to $500 for community events in the borough.

## Who can apply

- Groups run by volunteers who live in the borough.
- Events that sell alcohol cannot apply.

## What we fund

- Benefit to local residents.
- Inclusion and access, such as step-free routes, signs or quiet spaces.

## Conditions

- At least 20% of each item's cost must come from other funding.
- Groups report how the money was spent within two months of the event.
essentials/festival.handbook.md:
# Volunteer handbook

## Opening

Collect the key from the caretaker at 08:30. Unlock the side door and switch on the hall lights.

## Opening (old version)

Collect the key at 08:30 and unlock the side door. Ask the caretaker for the alarm code before you go in.

## Setup

Put out the tables and gazebos by 10:00. Keep every path 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs. Volunteers bring water and a hat, because shade is limited.

## Stalls

Each stall shows its prices and allergy labels. No stall sells alcohol.

## Fire safety

Keep the fire exits clear. The extinguishers are by the side door and in the kitchen.

Emergency contacts: call 112 in an emergency. Site lead: 07700 900123.

## First aid

The first aid kit is in the hall office. Write every treatment in the log book.

Emergency contacts: call 112 in an emergency. Site lead: 07700 900123.

## Lost children

Bring a lost child to the information tent. Never take a child off the site.

Emergency contacts: call the site lead first on 07700 900123, then 112 if the child is not found within 10 minutes.

## Closing

Lock the side door at 18:00. Return the key to the caretaker.

## Contact

For rota changes, email `rota@example.org`.

essentials/festival.council-summary.md:
# Summary for the council

This is a summary of last year's festival for the council. Last year's festival was a great success for the neighbourhood, and we want to tell the council about it in this summary.

Last year 200 people came to the festival. That is 200 attendees, which we think is a very good number for a first festival. Many of the 200 attendees were families from the streets nearby.

Our income last year was $900. This income came from stall fees and donations on the day. The $900 of income was more than we expected when we started planning.

Our expenses last year were $650. The expenses were for the venue, tables, gazebos, signs and the first aid kit. We kept the $650 of expenses low because volunteers did most of the work.

This means that last year we had a surplus of $250. The surplus of $250 is the difference between our income of $900 and our expenses of $650. We have kept the $250 surplus to help pay for this year's festival.

The festival was run by volunteers. All the work was done by volunteers, and no one was paid. Our volunteers set up the stalls, ran the information tent and cleaned up at the end of the day.

People told us they enjoyed the music, the food and meeting their neighbours. Some people told us the day was hot and there was not much shade. Some people told us the food queues were long. We have listened to what people told us.

This year we want to make the festival even better. This year we want to make it more accessible, with step-free routes, clear signs and a quiet space. We think the council will agree that this is important.

To sum up, last year's festival had 200 attendees, $900 of income, $650 of expenses and a surplus of $250. It was run by volunteers, and people enjoyed it. We hope the council will support us again this year, and we thank the council for reading this summary.

essentials/festival.council/rules-2024.md:
# Council event rules, 2024

1. Events with fewer than 150 people on private land need no event permit.
2. Road closures need six weeks' notice to the council.
3. Every food stall needs a temporary food licence.
essentials/festival.council/update-2026.md:
# Council event rules: update from 1 March 2026

1. Any outdoor community event with more than 100 people needs an event permit, on public or private land. This replaces rule 1 of the 2024 rules.
2. Events on school grounds also need the school's written consent.
3. The other 2024 rules still apply.

This is a summary of last year's festival for the council. Last year's festival was a great success for the neighbourhood, and we want to tell the council about it in this summary.

Last year 200 people came to the festival. That is 200 attendees, which we think is a very good number for a first festival. Many of the 200 attendees were families from the streets nearby.

Our income last year was $900. This income came from stall fees and donations on the day. The $900 of income was more than we expected when we started planning.

Our expenses last year were $650. The expenses were for the venue, tables, gazebos, signs and the first aid kit. We kept the $650 of expenses low because volunteers did most of the work.

This means that last year we had a surplus of $250. The surplus of $250 is the difference between our income of $900 and our expenses of $650. We have kept the $250 surplus to help pay for this year's festival.

The festival was run by volunteers. All the work was done by volunteers, and no one was paid. Our volunteers set up the stalls, ran the information tent and cleaned up at the end of the day.

People told us they enjoyed the music, the food and meeting their neighbours. Some people told us the day was hot and there was not much shade. Some people told us the food queues were long. We have listened to what people told us.

This year we want to make the festival even better. This year we want to make it more accessible, with step-free routes, clear signs and a quiet space. We think the council will agree that this is important.

To sum up, last year's festival had 200 attendees, $900 of income, $650 of expenses and a surplus of $250. It was run by volunteers, and people enjoyed it. We hope the council will support us again this year, and we thank the council for reading this summary.

# Decisions

Settled on 4 May 2026.

## The festival

- Free, and one day: Saturday 27 June 2026.
- For about 120 neighbours.
- Budget: $1,000.
- Step-free access for everyone.
- No alcohol.
- Run by volunteers.

## Name

Common Ground. It shares its name with the Common Ground Café; the café's owner is happy to share it.

## Venue

The School: $180, capacity 160, step-free, with an indoor backup for rain. The Hall holds only 80 people, and the Park has no rain cover.

## Programme

- Music: the school band until 16:00, and nothing amplified after 17:00. Reason: not given.
- Food: two stalls, allergy labels on everything, and no alcohol. Reason: not given.

## Parked

- Kids' area: parked until we know how many volunteers we have. The volunteer count reopens it.

Grants of up to $500 for community events in the borough.

## Who can apply

- Groups run by volunteers who live in the borough.
- Events that sell alcohol cannot apply.

- Benefit to local residents.

essentials/festival:3.handbook.md:
# Volunteer handbook

## Opening

Collect the key from the caretaker at 08:30. Unlock the side door and switch on the hall lights.

## Opening (old version)

Collect the key at 08:30 and unlock the side door. Ask the caretaker for the alarm code before you go in.

## Setup

Put out the tables and gazebos by 10:00. Keep every path 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs. Volunteers bring water and a hat, because shade is limited.

## Stalls

Each stall shows its prices and allergy labels. No stall sells alcohol.

## Fire safety

Keep the fire exits clear. The extinguishers are by the side door and in the kitchen.

Emergency contacts: call 112 in an emergency. Site lead: 07700 900123.

## First aid

The first aid kit is in the hall office. Write every treatment in the log book.

Emergency contacts: call 112 in an emergency. Site lead: 07700 900123.

## Lost children

Bring a lost child to the information tent. Never take a child off the site.

Emergency contacts: call the site lead first on 07700 900123, then 112 if the child is not found within 10 minutes.

## Closing

Lock the side door at 18:00. Return the key to the caretaker.

## Contact

For rota changes, email `rota@example.org`.

essentials/festival:3.design.md:
# Design: Common Ground at the School

Status: not yet approved by the residents' group. An independent reviewer checked it on 11 May 2026; its findings are fixed below or listed under Open questions.

## Purpose

A free, one-day festival for about 120 neighbours on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000, with step-free access for everyone, run by volunteers. The day goes well if about 120 people come, we stay within budget and nobody reports an access problem.

## Scope

- In: the layout, the timetable, the rain plan and the volunteer roles.
- Out: bookings, the permit application, publicity, and the kids' area, which is parked.

## Layout

- The main gate is the step-free entrance, with the information tent beside it.
- The band plays at the far end of the playground, away from the houses.
- The two food stalls stand along the playground's side wall, with their queues marked away from the main path.
- Shaded seating under gazebos sits between the band and the stalls.
- The first aid point is in the hall office, signed from the gate.
- Every path stays 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs.

## Timetable

| Time | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 09:00 | Volunteers arrive and set up |
| 11:00 | Gates and food stalls open |
| 12:00 to 16:00 | The school band plays, with breaks |
| 16:00 to 17:00 | A quiet hour: no live music |
| 17:00 | Gates and stalls close; nothing amplified after this |
| 17:00 to 18:00 | Pack-up |
| 18:00 | The site is locked |

## Rain plan

- The site lead decides at 08:00 on the day, from the forecast, and again at 13:00 if rain starts.
- If it rains, the band and the seating move into the school hall, the indoor backup.
- The food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors. Nothing is cooked indoors.
- Stewards hold the hall at its safe number of people and run a queue at its door.
- Signs at the gate point to the hall's entrance.

## Volunteer roles

- Site lead: one, all day. Makes the rain call and the decisions on the day, and handles emergencies.
- Stewards: the gate, the paths and the hall door.
- Stalls: help stallholders set up and check allergy labels.
- First aid: staff the first aid point and keep the log book.

## Decisions

- The band plays at the far end of the playground, so its sound faces away from the houses.
- Nothing is cooked indoors, so the hall stays safe and the school's kitchen is not needed.
- The rain call is made twice, at 08:00 and 13:00, because summer showers often start in the afternoon.
- Everyone uses one step-free entrance, so nobody is sent to a different door.
- Each food stall needs a temporary food licence (council/rules-2024.md, rule 3).

## Failure paths

- Rain: the rain plan above.
- Heat: shaded seating and water; volunteers bring water and a hat.
- Too many people: stewards count at the gate and hold entry at the site's capacity of 160.
- A lost child: the Lost children section of the volunteer handbook.

## Checks

- Every path is 1.5 metres wide: walk it with a tape measure on setup day.
- Amplified sound stays inside its limits: the site lead checks at 16:00 and 17:00.
- The rain plan works: a site visit with the caretaker confirms the hall's safe number and its step-free route.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold. sources.md gives 160 for the whole site, not for the hall. Ask the caretaker.
- Whether the hall's entrance is step-free. Check it on the site visit.
- Whether the event needs a permit, and what form the school's consent takes. Ask the council's events officer.
essentials/festival:3.plan.md:
# Preparation plan

Status: approved by the residents' group on 11 May 2026.

Goal: everything is ready for Common Ground on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000 and the limits in decisions.md.

Out of scope: the kids' area, which is parked, and publicity beyond the volunteer and council documents.

## Steps

- [ ] 1. Ask the council's events officer about the permit and the school's consent. Owner: chair. Depends on: nothing. Check: written answers.
- [ ] 2. Apply for the event permit, if one is needed. Owner: chair. Depends on: 1. Check: the council's confirmation.
- [ ] 3. Get the school's written consent. Owner: chair. Depends on: 1. Check: the signed consent.
- [ ] 4. Book the School. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: 3. Check: the school's booking confirmation.
- [ ] 5. Get a temporary food licence for each stall. Owner: stalls lead. Depends on: 4. Check: two licences.
- [ ] 6. Confirm the school band until 16:00. Owner: chair. Depends on: 4. Check: the band leader's reply.
- [ ] 7. Fill the volunteer rota: 14 volunteers, three-hour shifts, nobody under 16 alone. Owner: volunteer coordinator. Depends on: 4. Check: every shift filled, with nobody under 16 alone.
- [ ] 8. Prepare the volunteer documents: the handbook, the welcome page and the role pages. Owner: volunteer coordinator. Depends on: 7. Check: the pages exist, and the role pages give the shift times.
- [ ] 9. Send the council a summary of last year, under 150 words. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: nothing. Check: under 150 words, with last year's four figures.
- [ ] 10. Visit the site with the caretaker: the hall's safe number and its step-free route. Owner: site lead. Depends on: 4. Check: both written in design.md.
- [ ] 11. Run the day. Owner: site lead. Depends on: all the steps above.
- [ ] 12. After the day, collect feedback and close the accounts. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: 11. Check: feedback saved, and the accounts within $1,000.

## Risks

- The permit takes longer than expected. Step 1 comes first, so there is time to ask.
- Too few volunteers for every shift. Step 7 shows it before the day, and the kids' area stays parked.
- Rain. The rain plan is in design.md, and step 10 confirms how many people the hall holds.

## Challenge

The weakest link is the permit and the school's consent: every step after 4 depends on them, so the plan asks about them first. How many people the hall holds stays unknown until step 10.

Thank you for helping at our neighbourhood festival! You will receive your shift by email a week before the day.

On the day, come to the information tent at the school gate. Wear the green T-shirt we give you.

essentials/festival:4.council-summary.md:
# Summary for the council

Last year's neighbourhood festival was run entirely by volunteers.

- Attendees: 200.
- Income: $900, from stall fees and donations.
- Expenses: $650, for the venue, tables, gazebos, signs and first aid.
- Surplus: $250, kept for this year's festival.

People enjoyed the music, the food and meeting their neighbours. They told us the day was hot, with little shade, and that the food queues were long.

This year we want to make the festival more accessible, with step-free routes, clear signs and a quiet space. We hope the council will support us again.

essentials/festival:4.decisions.md:
# Decisions

Settled on 4 May 2026.

## The festival

- Free, and one day: Saturday 27 June 2026.
- For about 120 neighbours.
- Budget: $1,000.
- Step-free access for everyone.
- No alcohol.
- Run by volunteers.

## Name

Common Ground. It shares its name with the Common Ground Café; the café's owner is happy to share it.

## Venue

The School: $180, capacity 160, step-free, with an indoor backup for rain. The Hall holds only 80 people, and the Park has no rain cover.

## Programme

- Music: the school band until 16:00, and nothing amplified after 17:00. Reason: not given.
- Food: two stalls, allergy labels on everything, and no alcohol. Reason: not given.

## Volunteers

Settled on 11 May 2026.

- 14 volunteers.
- Shifts are three hours long.
- Nobody under 16 works alone.
- Roles: stewards, stalls and first aid, with one site lead on duty all day.
- Every volunteer gets a short briefing before their first shift.

## Shifts

Settled on 15 June 2026.

- Three shifts: 09:00 to 12:00, 12:00 to 15:00 and 15:00 to 18:00.

## Permit

From the council's events officer, on 8 June 2026.

- The permit fee is waived for free events.
- The school's consent goes on form EV2, signed by the head teacher.
- Apply at least two weeks before the event: by Saturday 13 June 2026.

## Parked

- Kids' area: parked until we know how many volunteers we have. We now know there are 14; it is not reopened yet.
essentials/festival:4.design.md:
# Design: Common Ground at the School

Status: not yet approved by the residents' group. An independent reviewer checked it on 11 May 2026; its findings are fixed below or listed under Open questions.

## Purpose

A free, one-day festival for about 120 neighbours on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000, with step-free access for everyone, run by volunteers. The day goes well if about 120 people come, we stay within budget and nobody reports an access problem.

## Scope

- In: the layout, the timetable, the rain plan and the volunteer roles.
- Out: bookings, the permit application, publicity, and the kids' area, which is parked.

## Layout

- The main gate is the step-free entrance, with the information tent beside it.
- The band plays at the far end of the playground, away from the houses.
- The two food stalls stand along the playground's side wall, with their queues marked away from the main path.
- Shaded seating under gazebos sits between the band and the stalls.
- The first aid point is in the hall office, signed from the gate.
- Every path stays 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs.

## Timetable

| Time | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 09:00 | Volunteers arrive and set up |
| 11:00 | Gates and food stalls open |
| 12:00 to 16:00 | The school band plays, with breaks |
| 16:00 to 17:00 | A quiet hour: no live music |
| 17:00 | Gates and stalls close; nothing amplified after this |
| 17:00 to 18:00 | Pack-up |
| 18:00 | The site is locked |

## Rain plan

- The site lead decides at 08:00 on the day, from the forecast, and again at 13:00 if rain starts.
- If it rains, the band and the seating move into the school hall, the indoor backup.
- The food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors. Nothing is cooked indoors.
- Stewards hold the hall at its safe number of people and run a queue at its door.
- Signs at the gate point to the hall's entrance.

## Volunteer roles

- Site lead: one, all day. Makes the rain call and the decisions on the day, and handles emergencies.
- Stewards: the gate, the paths and the hall door.
- Stalls: help stallholders set up and check allergy labels.
- First aid: staff the first aid point and keep the log book.

## Decisions

- The band plays at the far end of the playground, so its sound faces away from the houses.
- Nothing is cooked indoors, so the hall stays safe and the school's kitchen is not needed.
- The rain call is made twice, at 08:00 and 13:00, because summer showers often start in the afternoon.
- Everyone uses one step-free entrance, so nobody is sent to a different door.
- Each food stall needs a temporary food licence (council/rules-2024.md, rule 3).

## Failure paths

- Rain: the rain plan above.
- Heat: shaded seating and water; volunteers bring water and a hat.
- Too many people: stewards count at the gate and hold entry at the site's capacity of 160.
- A lost child: the Lost children section of the volunteer handbook.

## Checks

- Every path is 1.5 metres wide: walk it with a tape measure on setup day.
- Amplified sound stays inside its limits: the site lead checks at 16:00 and 17:00.
- The rain plan works: a site visit with the caretaker confirms the hall's safe number and its step-free route.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold. sources.md gives 160 for the whole site, not for the hall. Ask the caretaker.
- Whether the hall's entrance is step-free. Check it on the site visit.
- Whether the event needs a permit, and what form the school's consent takes. Ask the council's events officer.
essentials/festival:4.plan.md:
# Preparation plan

Status: approved by the residents' group on 11 May 2026.

Goal: everything is ready for Common Ground on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000 and the limits in decisions.md.

Out of scope: the kids' area, which is parked, and publicity beyond the volunteer and council documents.

## Steps

- [ ] 1. Ask the council's events officer about the permit and the school's consent. Owner: chair. Depends on: nothing. Check: written answers.
- [ ] 2. Apply for the event permit, if one is needed. Owner: chair. Depends on: 1. Check: the council's confirmation.
- [ ] 3. Get the school's written consent. Owner: chair. Depends on: 1. Check: the signed consent.
- [ ] 4. Book the School. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: 3. Check: the school's booking confirmation.
- [ ] 5. Get a temporary food licence for each stall. Owner: stalls lead. Depends on: 4. Check: two licences.
- [ ] 6. Confirm the school band until 16:00. Owner: chair. Depends on: 4. Check: the band leader's reply.
- [ ] 7. Fill the volunteer rota: 14 volunteers, three-hour shifts, nobody under 16 alone. Owner: volunteer coordinator. Depends on: 4. Check: every shift filled, with nobody under 16 alone.
- [ ] 8. Prepare the volunteer documents: the handbook, the welcome page and the role pages. Owner: volunteer coordinator. Depends on: 7. Check: the pages exist, and the role pages give the shift times.
- [ ] 9. Send the council a summary of last year, under 150 words. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: nothing. Check: under 150 words, with last year's four figures.
- [ ] 10. Visit the site with the caretaker: the hall's safe number and its step-free route. Owner: site lead. Depends on: 4. Check: both written in design.md.
- [ ] 11. Run the day. Owner: site lead. Depends on: all the steps above.
- [ ] 12. After the day, collect feedback and close the accounts. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: 11. Check: feedback saved, and the accounts within $1,000.

## Risks

- The permit takes longer than expected. Step 1 comes first, so there is time to ask.
- Too few volunteers for every shift. Step 7 shows it before the day, and the kids' area stays parked.
- Rain. The rain plan is in design.md, and step 10 confirms how many people the hall holds.

## Challenge

The weakest link is the permit and the school's consent: every step after 4 depends on them, so the plan asks about them first. How many people the hall holds stays unknown until step 10.

Grants of up to $500 for community events in the borough.

- Groups report how the money was spent within two months of the event.

essentials/festival:5.council-summary.md:
# Summary for the council

This is a summary of last year's festival for the council. Last year's festival was a great success for the neighbourhood, and we want to tell the council about it in this summary.

Last year 200 people came to the festival. That is 200 attendees, which we think is a very good number for a first festival. Many of the 200 attendees were families from the streets nearby.

Our income last year was $900. This income came from stall fees and donations on the day. The $900 of income was more than we expected when we started planning.

Our expenses last year were $650. The expenses were for the venue, tables, gazebos, signs and the first aid kit. We kept the $650 of expenses low because volunteers did most of the work.

This means that last year we had a surplus of $250. The surplus of $250 is the difference between our income of $900 and our expenses of $650. We have kept the $250 surplus to help pay for this year's festival.

The festival was run by volunteers. All the work was done by volunteers, and no one was paid. Our volunteers set up the stalls, ran the information tent and cleaned up at the end of the day.

People told us they enjoyed the music, the food and meeting their neighbours. Some people told us the day was hot and there was not much shade. Some people told us the food queues were long. We have listened to what people told us.

This year we want to make the festival even better. This year we want to make it more accessible, with step-free routes, clear signs and a quiet space. We think the council will agree that this is important.

To sum up, last year's festival had 200 attendees, $900 of income, $650 of expenses and a surplus of $250. It was run by volunteers, and people enjoyed it. We hope the council will support us again this year, and we thank the council for reading this summary.

essentials/festival:5.decisions.md:
# Decisions

Settled on 4 May 2026.

## The festival

- Free, and one day: Saturday 27 June 2026.
- For about 120 neighbours.
- Budget: $1,000.
- Step-free access for everyone.
- No alcohol.
- Run by volunteers.

## Name

Common Ground. It shares its name with the Common Ground Café; the café's owner is happy to share it.

## Venue

The School: $180, capacity 160, step-free, with an indoor backup for rain. The Hall holds only 80 people, and the Park has no rain cover.

## Programme

- Music: the school band until 16:00, and nothing amplified after 17:00. Reason: not given.
- Food: two stalls, allergy labels on everything, and no alcohol. Reason: not given.

## Volunteers

Settled on 11 May 2026.

- 14 volunteers.
- Shifts are three hours long.
- Nobody under 16 works alone.
- Roles: stewards, stalls and first aid, with one site lead on duty all day.
- Every volunteer gets a short briefing before their first shift.

## Shifts

Settled on 15 June 2026.

- Three shifts: 09:00 to 12:00, 12:00 to 15:00 and 15:00 to 18:00.

## Permit

From the council's events officer, on 8 June 2026.

- The permit fee is waived for free events.
- The school's consent goes on form EV2, signed by the head teacher.
- Apply at least two weeks before the event: by Saturday 13 June 2026.

## Parked

- Kids' area: parked until we know how many volunteers we have. We now know there are 14; it is not reopened yet.
essentials/festival:5.design.md:
# Design: Common Ground at the School

Status: not yet approved by the residents' group. An independent reviewer checked it on 11 May 2026; its findings are fixed below or listed under Open questions.

## Purpose

A free, one-day festival for about 120 neighbours on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000, with step-free access for everyone, run by volunteers. The day goes well if about 120 people come, we stay within budget and nobody reports an access problem.

## Scope

- In: the layout, the timetable, the rain plan and the volunteer roles.
- Out: bookings, the permit application, publicity, and the kids' area, which is parked.

## Layout

- The main gate is the step-free entrance, with the information tent beside it.
- The band plays at the far end of the playground, away from the houses.
- The two food stalls stand along the playground's side wall, with their queues marked away from the main path.
- Shaded seating under gazebos sits between the band and the stalls.
- The first aid point is in the hall office, signed from the gate.
- Every path stays 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs.

## Timetable

| Time | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 09:00 | Volunteers arrive and set up |
| 11:00 | Gates and food stalls open |
| 12:00 to 16:00 | The school band plays, with breaks |
| 16:00 to 17:00 | A quiet hour: no live music |
| 17:00 | Gates and stalls close; nothing amplified after this |
| 17:00 to 18:00 | Pack-up |
| 18:00 | The site is locked |

## Rain plan

- The site lead decides at 08:00 on the day, from the forecast, and again at 13:00 if rain starts.
- If it rains, the band and the seating move into the school hall, the indoor backup.
- The food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors. Nothing is cooked indoors.
- Stewards hold the hall at its safe number of people and run a queue at its door.
- Signs at the gate point to the hall's entrance.

## Volunteer roles

- Site lead: one, all day. Makes the rain call and the decisions on the day, and handles emergencies.
- Stewards: the gate, the paths and the hall door.
- Stalls: help stallholders set up and check allergy labels.
- First aid: staff the first aid point and keep the log book.

## Decisions

- The band plays at the far end of the playground, so its sound faces away from the houses.
- Nothing is cooked indoors, so the hall stays safe and the school's kitchen is not needed.
- The rain call is made twice, at 08:00 and 13:00, because summer showers often start in the afternoon.
- Everyone uses one step-free entrance, so nobody is sent to a different door.
- Each food stall needs a temporary food licence (council/rules-2024.md, rule 3).

## Failure paths

- Rain: the rain plan above.
- Heat: shaded seating and water; volunteers bring water and a hat.
- Too many people: stewards count at the gate and hold entry at the site's capacity of 160.
- A lost child: the Lost children section of the volunteer handbook.

## Checks

- Every path is 1.5 metres wide: walk it with a tape measure on setup day.
- Amplified sound stays inside its limits: the site lead checks at 16:00 and 17:00.
- The rain plan works: a site visit with the caretaker confirms the hall's safe number and its step-free route.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold. sources.md gives 160 for the whole site, not for the hall. Ask the caretaker.
- Whether the hall's entrance is step-free. Check it on the site visit.
- Whether the event needs a permit, and what form the school's consent takes. Ask the council's events officer.
essentials/festival:5.plan.md:
# Preparation plan

Status: approved by the residents' group on 11 May 2026.

Goal: everything is ready for Common Ground on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000 and the limits in decisions.md.

Out of scope: the kids' area, which is parked, and publicity beyond the volunteer and council documents.

## Steps

- [x] 1. Ask the council's events officer about the permit and the school's consent. Owner: chair. Depends on: nothing. Check: written answers.
- [x] 2. Apply for the event permit, if one is needed. Owner: chair. Depends on: 1. Check: the council's confirmation.
- [x] 3. Get the school's written consent. Owner: chair. Depends on: 1. Check: the signed consent.
- [x] 4. Book the School. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: 3. Check: the school's booking confirmation.
- [x] 5. Get a temporary food licence for each stall. Owner: stalls lead. Depends on: 4. Check: two licences.
- [x] 6. Confirm the school band until 16:00. Owner: chair. Depends on: 4. Check: the band leader's reply.
- [x] 7. Fill the volunteer rota: 14 volunteers, three-hour shifts, nobody under 16 alone. Owner: volunteer coordinator. Depends on: 4. Check: every shift filled, with nobody under 16 alone.
- [x] 8. Prepare the volunteer documents: the handbook, the welcome page and the role pages. Owner: volunteer coordinator. Depends on: 7. Check: the pages exist, and the role pages give the shift times.
- [x] 9. Send the council a summary of last year, under 150 words. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: nothing. Check: under 150 words, with last year's four figures.
- [ ] 10. Visit the site with the caretaker: the hall's safe number and its step-free route. Owner: site lead. Depends on: 4. Check: both written in design.md.
- [x] 11. Run the day. Owner: site lead. Depends on: all the steps above.
- [ ] 12. After the day, collect feedback and close the accounts. Owner: treasurer. Depends on: 11. Check: feedback saved, and the accounts within $1,000.

## Risks

- The permit takes longer than expected. Step 1 comes first, so there is time to ask.
- Too few volunteers for every shift. Step 7 shows it before the day, and the kids' area stays parked.
- Rain. The rain plan is in design.md, and step 10 confirms how many people the hall holds.

## Challenge

The weakest link is the permit and the school's consent: every step after 4 depends on them, so the plan asks about them first. How many people the hall holds stays unknown until step 10.

1. Collect the key from the caretaker at 08:30.
2. Ask the caretaker for the alarm code before you go in.
3. Unlock the side door and switch on the hall lights.

In an emergency, use the [emergency contacts](emergency-contacts.md).

Emergency contacts: call the site lead first on 07700 900123, then 112 if the child is not found within 10 minutes.

essentials/festival:5.handbook/safety.md:
# Safety

Three pages cover safety on the day:

- [Fire safety](fire-safety.md): the fire exits and the extinguishers.

# Design: Common Ground at the School

Status: not yet approved by the residents' group. Fresh independent review completed; approval is pending.

## Purpose

A free, one-day festival for about 120 neighbours on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000, with step-free access for everyone, run by volunteers. No alcohol is sold or served. The day goes well if about 120 people come, we stay within budget and nobody reports an access problem.

## Scope

- In: the layout, the timetable, the rain plan and the volunteer roles.
- Out: bookings, the permit application, publicity, and the kids' area, which is parked.

## Layout

- The main gate is the step-free entrance, with the information tent beside it.
- The band plays at the far end of the playground, away from the houses.
- The two food stalls stand along the playground's side wall, with their queues marked away from the main path.
- Shaded seating under gazebos sits between the band and the stalls.
- The first aid point is in the hall office, signed from the gate.
- Every path stays 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs.

## Timetable

| Time | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 09:00 | Volunteers arrive and set up |
| 11:00 | Gates and food stalls open |
| 12:00 to 16:00 | The school band plays, with breaks |
| 16:00 to 17:00 | A quiet hour: no live music |
| 17:00 | Gates and stalls close; nothing amplified after this |
| 17:00 to 18:00 | Pack-up |
| 18:00 | The site is locked |

## Rain plan

- The site lead decides at 08:00 on the day, from the forecast, and again at 13:00 if rain starts.
- If it rains, the band and the seating move into the school hall, the indoor backup.
- The food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors. Nothing is cooked indoors.
- Stewards hold the hall at its safe number of people and run a queue at its door.
- Signs at the gate point to the hall's entrance.

## Volunteer roles

- Site lead: one, all day. Makes the rain call and the decisions on the day, and handles emergencies.
- Stewards: the gate, the paths and the hall door.
- Stalls: help stallholders set up and check allergy labels.
- First aid: staff the first aid point and keep the log book.

## Decisions

- The band plays at the far end of the playground, so its sound faces away from the houses.
- Nothing is cooked indoors, so the hall stays safe and the school's kitchen is not needed.
- The first rain call is at 08:00 so the site lead can choose the setup before volunteers arrive at 09:00. The 13:00 check lets the lead change the afternoon arrangement if rain starts after opening.
- Everyone uses one step-free entrance, so nobody is sent to a different door.
- The timetable keeps the settled limits: the band ends at 16:00 and nothing is amplified after 17:00 (decisions.md). Its other fixed points come from handbook.md: setup done by 10:00, paths 1.5 metres wide, and the site locked at 18:00. The chosen times leave an hour's margin around each fixed point: volunteers arrive at 09:00, an hour before setup must be done; gates open at 11:00, an hour after it; and the band starts at 12:00, once the stalls have been open an hour.
- Each food stall needs a temporary food licence (council/rules-2024.md, rule 3).

## Failure paths

- Rain: the rain plan above.
- Heat: shaded seating and water; volunteers bring water and a hat.
- Too many people: stewards count at the gate and hold entry at the site's capacity of 160.
- A lost child: the Lost children section of the volunteer handbook.

## Checks

- Every path is 1.5 metres wide: walk it with a tape measure on setup day.
- Amplified sound stays inside its limits: the site lead checks at 16:00 and 17:00.
- The rain plan works: a site visit with the caretaker confirms the hall's safe number and its step-free route.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold. sources.md gives 160 for the whole site, not for the hall. Ask the caretaker.
- Whether the hall's entrance is step-free. Check it on the site visit.
- The event permit is required for more than 100 people under council/update-2026.md:3. Ask the events officer for the application form and deadline. Written school consent is also required; its actual approval is pending.

## Reasons for the detailed choices

- Main-gate information tent: newcomers find help on the step-free route rather than making a second trip.
- Band at the far end: sound faces away from homes; this is a proposed layout, to check with the School.
- Stalls by the wall and marked queues: queues can be separated from the main accessible path.
- Gazebo seating between activities: people can rest without crossing the busiest queues.
- First aid in the office: the handbook identifies the kit there; signs let visitors find it.
- 09:00 setup and 11:00 opening: a proposed two-hour preparation window; confirm it with the caretaker.
- Noon band start: leave the first hour after the 11:00 opening for arrivals and food before music begins; this is a proposed timetable choice within the settled 16:00 band limit.
- Band breaks and a 16:00 finish: respect the settled band limit and provide rest.
- Food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors in rain: keep cooking out of the hall while giving customers shelter near the indoor seating; the caretaker must check that queues leave the entrance clear.
- Quiet hour and 17:00 closing: respect the amplification limit and leave time to pack up.
- 18:00 locking: the existing handbook specifies that time.
- Separate site-lead, steward, stall and first-aid roles: each safety-critical job has an owner; staffing numbers remain unconfirmed until the volunteer interview.

## Source checks and limits

The handbook supplies opening, first aid and lost-child procedures. The Lost children procedure is: bring the child to the information tent, never take them off site, call the site lead on 07700 900123 first, then 112 if not found within ten minutes. This is kept distinct from the other emergency order.
Council/rules-2024.md states the temporary-food-licence requirement. The March 2026 update replaces the exemption: this event needs a permit because 120 is more than 100. Written school consent is required by the update. The form, deadline and actual consent are still open; no permission is invented.

Here is the rain plan in other words. If it rains, the event moves from the playground into the School's indoor backup. The School's site capacity is 160, which is enough for 120 on paper. But that figure covers the whole site. It does not tell us how many people the hall itself can hold, so the usable room and the route into it are still unchecked. That is why I would not read 160 as a promise that 120 people fit inside.

A simple way to picture the plan is the outdoor layout folding into a smaller indoor arrangement. Everything you planned outside has to fit into less space, and the space must still work for people who move slowly or use wheels. That is why exits and circulation should be kept clear first, before any space is given to stalls and music. If stalls and music are placed first, people may have no clear way to move, and the way out matters most when many people are inside.

Now the weak points, with the most serious first. The most serious is that the usable capacity with furniture in place is not checked. A room that holds 160 when empty may hold far fewer once tables and a band are inside. The remedy is to ask the School to confirm a layout for 120. The next is the step-free route in wet weather. Wet ground and doorways can make a route that works in dry weather hard to use, and step-free access is one of your settled choices, so the plan must still honour it indoors. The remedy is to verify the route on a site visit. A moderate risk is that queues could obstruct the exits, because a queue that forms indoors can run across a doorway. The remedy is to mark a queue route so that the doorways stay open.

# Design: Common Ground at the School

Status: not yet approved by the residents' group. Independent review is pending; the chair should arrange a fresh reviewer before approval.

## Purpose

A free, one-day festival for about 120 neighbours on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000, with step-free access for everyone, run by volunteers. No alcohol is sold or served. The day goes well if about 120 people come, we stay within budget and nobody reports an access problem.

## Scope

- In: the layout, the timetable, the rain plan and the volunteer roles.
- Out: bookings, the permit application, publicity, and the kids' area, which is parked.

## Layout

- The main gate is the step-free entrance, with the information tent beside it.
- The band plays at the far end of the playground, away from the houses.
- The two food stalls stand along the playground's side wall, with their queues marked away from the main path.
- Shaded seating under gazebos sits between the band and the stalls.
- The first aid point is in the hall office, signed from the gate.
- Every path stays 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs.

## Timetable

| Time | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 09:00 | Volunteers arrive and set up |
| 11:00 | Gates and food stalls open |
| 12:00 to 16:00 | The school band plays, with breaks |
| 16:00 to 17:00 | A quiet hour: no live music |
| 17:00 | Gates and stalls close; nothing amplified after this |
| 17:00 to 18:00 | Pack-up |
| 18:00 | The site is locked |

## Rain plan

- The site lead decides at 08:00 on the day, from the forecast, and again at 13:00 if rain starts.
- If it rains, the band and the seating move into the school hall, the indoor backup.
- The food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors. Nothing is cooked indoors.
- Stewards hold the hall at its safe number of people and run a queue at its door.
- Signs at the gate point to the hall's entrance.

## Volunteer roles

- Site lead: one, all day. Makes the rain call and the decisions on the day, and handles emergencies.
- Stewards: the gate, the paths and the hall door.
- Stalls: help stallholders set up and check allergy labels.
- First aid: staff the first aid point and keep the log book.

## Decisions

- The band plays at the far end of the playground, so its sound faces away from the houses.
- Nothing is cooked indoors, so the hall stays safe and the school's kitchen is not needed.
- The first rain call is at 08:00 so the site lead can choose the setup before volunteers arrive at 09:00. The 13:00 check lets the lead change the afternoon arrangement if rain starts after opening.
- Everyone uses one step-free entrance, so nobody is sent to a different door.
- The timetable keeps the settled limits: the band ends at 16:00 and nothing is amplified after 17:00 (decisions.md). Its other fixed points come from handbook.md: setup done by 10:00, paths 1.5 metres wide, and the site locked at 18:00. The chosen times leave an hour's margin around each fixed point: volunteers arrive at 09:00, an hour before setup must be done; gates open at 11:00, an hour after it; and the band starts at 12:00, once the stalls have been open an hour.
- Each food stall needs a temporary food licence (council/rules-2024.md, rule 3).

## Failure paths

- Rain: the rain plan above.
- Heat: shaded seating and water; volunteers bring water and a hat.
- Too many people: stewards count at the gate and hold entry at the site's capacity of 160.
- A lost child: the Lost children section of the volunteer handbook.

## Checks

- Every path is 1.5 metres wide: walk it with a tape measure on setup day.
- Amplified sound stays inside its limits: the site lead checks at 16:00 and 17:00.
- The rain plan works: a site visit with the caretaker confirms the hall's safe number and its step-free route.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold. sources.md gives 160 for the whole site, not for the hall. Ask the caretaker.
- Whether the hall's entrance is step-free. Check it on the site visit.
- The event permit is required for more than 100 people under council/update-2026.md:3. Ask the events officer for the application form and deadline. Written school consent is also required; its actual approval is pending.

## Reasons for the detailed choices

- Main-gate information tent: newcomers find help on the step-free route rather than making a second trip.
- Band at the far end: sound faces away from homes; this is a proposed layout, to check with the School.
- Stalls by the wall and marked queues: queues can be separated from the main accessible path.
- Gazebo seating between activities: people can rest without crossing the busiest queues.
- First aid in the office: the handbook identifies the kit there; signs let visitors find it.
- 09:00 setup and 11:00 opening: a proposed two-hour preparation window; confirm it with the caretaker.
- Noon band start: leave the first hour after the 11:00 opening for arrivals and food before music begins; this is a proposed timetable choice within the settled 16:00 band limit.
- Band breaks and a 16:00 finish: respect the settled band limit and provide rest.
- Food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors in rain: keep cooking out of the hall while giving customers shelter near the indoor seating; the caretaker must check that queues leave the entrance clear.
- Quiet hour and 17:00 closing: respect the amplification limit and leave time to pack up.
- 18:00 locking: the existing handbook specifies that time.
- Separate site-lead, steward, stall and first-aid roles: each safety-critical job has an owner; staffing numbers remain unconfirmed until the volunteer interview.

## Source checks and limits

The handbook supplies opening, first aid and lost-child procedures. The Lost children procedure is: bring the child to the information tent, never take them off site, call the site lead on 07700 900123 first, then 112 if not found within ten minutes. This is kept distinct from the other emergency order.
Council/rules-2024.md states the temporary-food-licence requirement. The March 2026 update replaces the exemption: this event needs a permit because 120 is more than 100. Written school consent is required by the update. The form, deadline and actual consent are still open; no permission is invented.

## Author reader check

Reader check: I assessed whether a builder with only design.md can carry out the proposal without this conversation. The layout, times, owners, source rules and checks are stated in the file; no instruction from the conversation is needed. The rain arrangement cannot be put into operation until the caretaker confirms hall capacity and the step-free route, and the events officer settles the permit procedure and written consent. These are named approval and source checks, not details for a builder to guess. Approval and those checks remain pending.

# Design: Common Ground at the School

Status: not yet approved by the residents' group. Independent review is pending; the chair should arrange a fresh reviewer before approval.

## Purpose

A free, one-day festival for about 120 neighbours on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000, with step-free access for everyone, run by volunteers. No alcohol is sold or served. The day goes well if about 120 people come, we stay within budget and nobody reports an access problem.

## Scope

- In: the layout, the timetable, the rain plan and the volunteer roles.
- Out: bookings, the permit application, publicity, and the kids' area, which is parked.

## Layout

- The main gate is the step-free entrance, with the information tent beside it.
- The band plays at the far end of the playground, away from the houses.
- The two food stalls stand along the playground's side wall, with their queues marked away from the main path.
- Shaded seating under gazebos sits between the band and the stalls.
- The first aid point is in the hall office, signed from the gate.
- Every path stays 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs.

## Timetable

| Time | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 09:00 | Volunteers arrive and set up |
| 11:00 | Gates and food stalls open |
| 12:00 to 16:00 | The school band plays, with breaks |
| 16:00 to 17:00 | A quiet hour: no live music |
| 17:00 | Gates and stalls close; nothing amplified after this |
| 17:00 to 18:00 | Pack-up |
| 18:00 | The site is locked |

## Rain plan

- The site lead decides at 08:00 on the day, from the forecast, and again at 13:00 if rain starts.
- If it rains, the band and the seating move into the school hall, the indoor backup.
- The food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors. Nothing is cooked indoors.
- Stewards hold the hall at its safe number of people and run a queue at its door.
- Signs at the gate point to the hall's entrance.

## Volunteer roles

- Site lead: one, all day. Makes the rain call and the decisions on the day, and handles emergencies.
- Stewards: the gate, the paths and the hall door.
- Stalls: help stallholders set up and check allergy labels.
- First aid: staff the first aid point and keep the log book.

## Decisions

- The band plays at the far end of the playground, so its sound faces away from the houses.
- Nothing is cooked indoors, so the hall stays safe and the school's kitchen is not needed.
- The rain call is made twice, at 08:00 and 13:00, because summer showers often start in the afternoon.
- Everyone uses one step-free entrance, so nobody is sent to a different door.
- Each food stall needs a temporary food licence (council/rules-2024.md, rule 3).

## Failure paths

- Rain: the rain plan above.
- Heat: shaded seating and water; volunteers bring water and a hat.
- Too many people: stewards count at the gate and hold entry at the site's capacity of 160.
- A lost child: the Lost children section of the volunteer handbook.

## Checks

- Every path is 1.5 metres wide: walk it with a tape measure on setup day.
- Amplified sound stays inside its limits: the site lead checks at 16:00 and 17:00.
- The rain plan works: a site visit with the caretaker confirms the hall's safe number and its step-free route.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold. sources.md gives 160 for the whole site, not for the hall. Ask the caretaker.
- Whether the hall's entrance is step-free. Check it on the site visit.
- The event permit is required for more than 100 people under council/update-2026.md:3. Ask the events officer for the application form and deadline. Written school consent is also required; its actual approval is pending.

## Reasons for the detailed choices

- Main-gate information tent: newcomers find help on the step-free route rather than making a second trip.
- Band at the far end: sound faces away from homes; this is a proposed layout, to check with the School.
- Stalls by the wall and marked queues: queues can be separated from the main accessible path.
- Gazebo seating between activities: people can rest without crossing the busiest queues.
- First aid in the office: the handbook identifies the kit there; signs let visitors find it.
- 09:00 setup and 11:00 opening: a proposed two-hour preparation window; confirm it with the caretaker.
- Band breaks and a 16:00 finish: respect the settled band limit and provide rest.
- Quiet hour and 17:00 closing: respect the amplification limit and leave time to pack up.
- 18:00 locking: the existing handbook specifies that time.
- Separate site-lead, steward, stall and first-aid roles: each safety-critical job has an owner; staffing numbers remain unconfirmed until the volunteer interview.

## Source checks and limits

The handbook supplies opening, first aid and lost-child procedures. The Lost children procedure is: bring the child to the information tent, never take them off site, call the site lead on 07700 900123 first, then 112 if not found within ten minutes. This is kept distinct from the other emergency order.
Council/rules-2024.md states the temporary-food-licence requirement. The March 2026 update replaces the exemption: this event needs a permit because 120 is more than 100. Written school consent is required by the update. The form, deadline and actual consent are still open; no permission is invented.

# Carryover: Common Ground festival

Written on Monday 22 June 2026. Independent cold read pending; the chair should arrange it. Approval pending. Read it whole before you act on it.

## Goal and state

We are preparing Common Ground, a free one-day festival for about 120 neighbours at the School on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000. The design, the plan and the volunteer documents are written. The work left is the group's own: the permit, the booking and the day itself, then feedback and the accounts.

## Structure and concepts

- decisions.md: everything the group has settled.
- design.md: the design of the day, with the rain plan. Not yet approved.
- plan.md: the approved preparation plan, as a checklist.
- handbook/: the volunteer handbook, one page per topic. Start at handbook/index.md.
- roles/: one page per volunteer role.
- AGENTS.md: the project's rules for agents.

## Working rules

- Work only in this project. Never send, publish or use real accounts (AGENTS.md).
- Every public notice shows the step-free entrance and the access contact (AGENTS.md).
- CSV files stay out of version control because they hold personal data, so deleting one cannot be undone.

## Done so far

- The handbook is split into topic pages, with a Safety page and an index: handbook/index.md.
- welcome.md gives the shift length, what to bring and whom to call.
- council-summary.md was trimmed in the earlier chapter, but the current checkpoint needs checking.
- old-signups.csv is deleted, with the group's approval. duplicate-contacts.csv is kept.
- The three role pages give the three shifts: roles/.
- The rule on public notices is in AGENTS.md.

## Decisions

All are in decisions.md, except one: the Lost children page keeps its own emergency order, the site lead first and then 112, on purpose.

## Remaining work

1. Steps 2 to 7 and 10 of plan.md: the group's own tasks, from the permit to the site visit. Only the group can confirm them.
2. Step 11: the day itself.
3. Step 12: after the day, collect feedback and close the accounts.

No approved agent work is left.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold, and whether its entrance is step-free: design.md, Open questions.
- The kids' area is still parked.
- Where volunteers park: no file says.

## References

- decisions.md, design.md, plan.md, handbook/index.md, roles/ and AGENTS.md.
- No temporary material is kept.

## First next step

Ask the group which steps of plan.md are done, and mark each one with its evidence.

## Written against

Branch main. Last commit: checkpoint for chapter 5; obtain its hash with git rev-parse HEAD. AGENTS.md and carryover.md are uncommitted.

# Carryover: Common Ground festival

Written on Monday 22 June 2026. Independent cold read pending; the chair should arrange it. Approval pending. Read it whole before you act on it.

## Goal and state

We are preparing Common Ground, a free one-day festival for about 120 neighbours at the School on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000. The design, the plan and the volunteer documents are written. The work left is the group's own: the permit, the booking and the day itself, then feedback and the accounts.

## Structure and concepts

- decisions.md: everything the group has settled.
- design.md: the design of the day, with the rain plan. Not yet approved.
- plan.md: the approved preparation plan, as a checklist.
- handbook/: the volunteer handbook, one page per topic. Start at handbook/index.md.
- roles/: one page per volunteer role.
- AGENTS.md: the project's rules for agents.

## Working rules

- Work only in this project. Never send, publish or use real accounts (AGENTS.md).
- Every public notice shows the step-free entrance and the access contact (AGENTS.md).
- CSV files stay out of version control because they hold personal data, so deleting one cannot be undone.

## Done so far

- The handbook is split into topic pages, with a Safety page and an index: handbook/index.md.
- welcome.md gives the shift length, what to bring and whom to call.
- council-summary.md was trimmed in the earlier chapter, but the current checkpoint needs checking.
- old-signups.csv is deleted, with the group's approval. duplicate-contacts.csv is kept.
- The three role pages give the three shifts: roles/.
- The rule on public notices is in AGENTS.md.

## Decisions

All are in decisions.md, except one: the Lost children page keeps its own emergency order, the site lead first and then 112, on purpose.

## Remaining work

1. Steps 2 to 7 and 10 of plan.md: the group's own tasks, from the permit to the site visit. Only the group can confirm them.
2. Step 11: the day itself.
3. Step 12: after the day, collect feedback and close the accounts.

No approved agent work is left.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold, and whether its entrance is step-free: design.md, Open questions.
- The kids' area is still parked.
- Where volunteers park: no file says.

## References

- decisions.md, design.md, plan.md, handbook/index.md, roles/ and AGENTS.md.
- No temporary material is kept.

## First next step

Ask the group which steps of plan.md are done, and mark each one with its evidence.

# Design: Common Ground at the School

Status: not yet approved by the residents' group. Independent review is pending; the chair should arrange a fresh reviewer before approval.

## Purpose

A free, one-day festival for about 120 neighbours on Saturday 27 June 2026, within $1,000, with step-free access for everyone, run by volunteers. No alcohol is sold or served. The day goes well if about 120 people come, we stay within budget and nobody reports an access problem.

## Scope

- In: the layout, the timetable, the rain plan and the volunteer roles.
- Out: bookings, the permit application, publicity, and the kids' area, which is parked.

## Layout

- The main gate is the step-free entrance, with the information tent beside it.
- The band plays at the far end of the playground, away from the houses.
- The two food stalls stand along the playground's side wall, with their queues marked away from the main path.
- Shaded seating under gazebos sits between the band and the stalls.
- The first aid point is in the hall office, signed from the gate.
- Every path stays 1.5 metres wide for wheelchairs.

## Timetable

| Time | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 09:00 | Volunteers arrive and set up |
| 11:00 | Gates and food stalls open |
| 12:00 to 16:00 | The school band plays, with breaks |
| 16:00 to 17:00 | A quiet hour: no live music |
| 17:00 | Gates and stalls close; nothing amplified after this |
| 17:00 to 18:00 | Pack-up |
| 18:00 | The site is locked |

## Rain plan

- The site lead decides at 08:00 on the day, from the forecast, and again at 13:00 if rain starts.
- If it rains, the band and the seating move into the school hall, the indoor backup.
- The food stalls stay outside under gazebos by the hall doors. Nothing is cooked indoors.
- Stewards hold the hall at its safe number of people and run a queue at its door.
- Signs at the gate point to the hall's entrance.

## Volunteer roles

- Site lead: one, all day. Makes the rain call and the decisions on the day, and handles emergencies.
- Stewards: the gate, the paths and the hall door.
- Stalls: help stallholders set up and check allergy labels.
- First aid: staff the first aid point and keep the log book.

## Decisions

- The band plays at the far end of the playground, so its sound faces away from the houses.
- Nothing is cooked indoors, so the hall stays safe and the school's kitchen is not needed.
- The rain call is made twice, at 08:00 and 13:00, because summer showers often start in the afternoon.
- Everyone uses one step-free entrance, so nobody is sent to a different door.
- Each food stall needs a temporary food licence (council/rules-2024.md, rule 3).

## Failure paths

- Rain: the rain plan above.
- Heat: shaded seating and water; volunteers bring water and a hat.
- Too many people: stewards count at the gate and hold entry at the site's capacity of 160.
- A lost child: the Lost children section of the volunteer handbook.

## Checks

- Every path is 1.5 metres wide: walk it with a tape measure on setup day.
- Amplified sound stays inside its limits: the site lead checks at 16:00 and 17:00.
- The rain plan works: a site visit with the caretaker confirms the hall's safe number and its step-free route.

## Open questions

- How many people the hall can safely hold. sources.md gives 160 for the whole site, not for the hall. Ask the caretaker.
- Whether the hall's entrance is step-free. Check it on the site visit.
- The event permit is required for more than 100 people under council/update-2026.md:3. Ask the events officer for the application form and deadline. Written school consent is also required; its actual approval is pending.

## Reasons for the detailed choices

- Main-gate information tent: newcomers find help on the step-free route rather than making a second trip.
- Band at the far end: sound faces away from homes; this is a proposed layout, to check with the School.
- Stalls by the wall and marked queues: queues can be separated from the main accessible path.
- Gazebo seating between activities: people can rest without crossing the busiest queues.
- First aid in the office: the handbook identifies the kit there; signs let visitors find it.
- 09:00 setup and 11:00 opening: a proposed two-hour preparation window; confirm it with the caretaker.
- Band breaks and a 16:00 finish: respect the settled band limit and provide rest.
- Quiet hour and 17:00 closing: respect the amplification limit and leave time to pack up.
- 18:00 locking: the existing handbook specifies that time.
- Separate site-lead, steward, stall and first-aid roles: each safety-critical job has an owner; staffing numbers remain unconfirmed until the volunteer interview.

## Source checks and limits

The handbook supplies opening, first aid and lost-child procedures. The Lost children procedure is: bring the child to the information tent, never take them off site, call the site lead on 07700 900123 first, then 112 if not found within ten minutes. This is kept distinct from the other emergency order.
Council/rules-2024.md states the temporary-food-licence requirement. The March 2026 update replaces the exemption: this event needs a permit because 120 is more than 100. Written school consent is required by the update. The form, deadline and actual consent are still open; no permission is invented.

# Summary for the council

Last year's neighbourhood festival was run entirely by volunteers.

- Attendees: 200.
- Income: $900, from stall fees and donations.
- Expenses: $650, for the venue, tables, gazebos, signs and first aid.
- Surplus: $250, kept for this year's festival.

This year we want to make the festival more accessible, with step-free routes, clear signs and a quiet space. We hope the council will support us again.

questionnaire when applicable
summary from the deep interview
The response, with its content, order and wording checked. There is no separate result.
each claim with evidence, whether confirmed, and who checked it, with evidence beside the claim
What was removed, what was kept with its location and reason, and what still needs approval to remove.

The output or work plan fitted to its reader, with the point first. For reworked material, also return the list of changes for approval, then the result and its check once the list is applied. The sizing check itself stays in thinking.

The material with missing parts added, and the gaps that could not be filled. The approval list gives each addition's source and reason, and each gap with what would settle it. The report after applying gives the result, its check and the gaps that remain.
The material with extra parts removed. The approval list gives each removal and why. The report after applying gives the result and its check.

The risk level and a short reason, with the four answers or a “plainly low” judgment. When the user asked about the risk, they see the level and the four answers in plain words, unless it is plainly low. Otherwise the task that asked decides what the user needs to see.
Each used method’s result and its actual status, returned to the task that asked for it.
The worker’s starting instructions and the report it must return. The task that asked for the brief sends it; writing it starts no worker.
The saved note with its actual review and approval status. On resuming, return the differences checked and the approved work that continues.
The actual work and check results, task status, cost where needed and cleanup results.
Each member’s answer with its name, a summary that keeps disagreements, and which answers are missing.
The approved changes, the final pass over the whole, actual check results and unfinished work.
Combined findings, how they were combined and who checked them, their actual check status, sources and coverage limits.
The proposed or approved instruction document, its location and whether it was actually saved.
Approved lessons and where they were saved, highlights dropped with reasons, and decisions still waiting for the user.
Approved changes and observed loading checks, recommendations, declined work and pending checks.

A short or full design with its actual approval status, such as "not yet approved", or ranked review findings. A full design also gives what its review found, how each finding was resolved, and any check still open.
Ranked findings with fixes, or a list of checks run when no problem was found. Mark unfinished checks. The design owner resolves findings before approval.
The one-line or full plan, its actual approval status, and the checklist showing which steps were checked when execution was allowed. A full plan also shows what its challenge found.

The grouping principle, each part’s boundary, each item’s place, and any missing or overlapping parts. After a change, also return the before-and-after map, checks, approvals and what was moved, changed or marked as replaced.
The view, how it will stay current and any requested tag edits. All other source content stays unchanged.
The new parent, what the selected items share, and where those items belong. Their content stays unchanged.
The combined account or proposal, a map of every original statement, updated references and items marked as replaced.
The shared part and working references to it. List copies with different meanings and leave them unchanged.
Parts, their boundaries and each item’s place, with any placement still unresolved.
The round of questions or the proposal, shown to the user, with the turn ended on it. When the user replies, each answer said back as accepted, changed, assumed or parked, by rule 4.
The earlier point, explained again to the user from the main idea to its details, with every reference in words.
The response or Markdown material, laid out for its reader.

The case, labelled one-sided: the precise position, reasons with their evidence and strength or marked as assumptions, the strongest objections each answered, conceded or met by narrowing, the weaknesses that still stand, how strong the case is and why, and the evidence that would strengthen or break it. The challenge's verdict is never part of the case.
The requested options or candidates. Add a comparison and a decision, or why the choice is set aside, only when a choice was requested.

Weak points that matter to the goal, including costs or risks even when success stays possible, each with its seriousness and remedy, then an honest verdict. When the user asked for the challenge, each assumption is marked checked or unchecked, and the most serious weakness comes first. When the challenge was not asked for, only the verdict and the serious weaknesses are shown, each with its reason, unless the user asks for more.
The summary of accepted, changed, assumed and parked items. The user has confirmed it, or got it in your final answer after telling you to start the work.
The question document, in the response by default for the user to send. Later, return its answers to clarification.
The visible “Going with” line, plus an offer of deep questions for parts whose answers depend on each other.
What was decided, set aside or passed to another task, with reasons. Include side topics and next steps; give the user the agreed summary.
The problem, goal, limits and test for a good answer, plus unknowns and what would settle them.

For an open name, the candidates, each with why it fits, or the chosen name and why. For a glossary change, the proposed entries. Add the rejected words with their reasons, and which existing terms and possible clashes you checked. Write or rename nothing here.

Sourced findings and their limits: an answer or claim verdict, compared candidates, or evidence for possible causes, returned to the task that asked for the research. The limits include what was looked for and not found, what was not covered and why, and what would change the answer.

The symptom, supported causes or marked hypotheses, rejected causes, and who should investigate or fix it next: the symptom with where, since when and how often it is seen; the chain from the symptom back to the trigger, each link with its evidence, confirmed or marked as a hypothesis; each cause ruled out with its evidence; and where a fix belongs, handed to the caller.
The answer or claim verdict, supporting and opposing evidence, limits and missing checks.

Candidates compared on the same terms, with sources, excluded and unexamined candidates, search coverage and dates: what counts, the terms, each fully compared candidate on each term with its evidence or "not found", each candidate screened out with why, where the search went and what it did not search, the survey's date and each source's date.

A comparison and recommendation, or no clear winner with what would settle it: the terms that matter, each option's values on the terms with its benefits, costs, risks and unknowns, the options dropped with reasons, why the recommended option beats the next best and how easily the choice can be undone, and the unknowns that would change it. Return options needing more development to the task that asked; do not start another brainstorm.
